<header class="ws-head"><span class="ws-kicker">Day 1 · 13:50–15:00 · Technical module 4 · serves M5</span><h2>Workflows, sync and who sees what<span class="ws-badge">Draft</span></h2><p class="ws-carries">What should happen next for this child, how does the record reach the server, and who is allowed to see it?</p></header>
<h3>Sessions</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Talk</span><span class="ws-sheet">13:50–14:00 · 10 min</span></span><b>Talk 3: Workflows, sync and who sees what</b><p>A short briefing before Lab 2. A plan definition says what should happen and when, such as the next vaccine due. Sync moves records between the device and the server. The gateway decides which records each user can reach.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Jing Tang · <span class="ws-t">Supports</span>Elly Nandi</p></div><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Lab</span><span class="ws-sheet">14:00–15:00 · 60 min</span></span><b>Lab 2: Sync data and run a workflow</b><p>In the Player, store records on the device and sync them to the server. Apply an immunization plan definition and see what comes due. Then sign in as two different users through the gateway and compare what each can see, for example 50 records against 10.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Elly Nandi, Fikri · <span class="ws-t">Supports</span>Jing Tang</p></div></div>
<h3>By the end you can</h3><ul><li>Sync records between the Player and the FHIR server</li><li>Read a plan definition and follow it through a workflow</li><li>Show that the gateway filters records by user</li></ul>
<h3>Where it meets the journey</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><b>Registered at home, and referred</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Everything Vilay records stays queued on the phone, for up to 28 days, and syncs when a signal returns.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>What happens to a queued registration if the clinic registers the same child before the phone syncs?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J3b/">J3b</a><b>Taifafeki vaccines are fitted to the Onesan schedule</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>The Onesan schedule (PlanDefinition) runs over every dose; at 10 weeks the 6-week doses come out overdue.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>How does the plan definition decide a dose is overdue, and what sets the date of the next one?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0b/">J4.0b</a><b>Dad creates a link to share at the clinic</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>The family's consent is recorded before the portal issues the link; the gateway enforces passcode, expiry and consent on every request.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>Where does the gateway read the consent from, and what does it do when the link has expired?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.1/">J4.1</a><b>A Taifafeki doctor sees the full history</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Each view is logged as an AuditEvent in Onesa, including failed passcode attempts.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>Which AuditEvent fields let Onesa tell the family who looked at the record, and when?</p></div></div>
<h3>Technical questions for the room</h3><ul class="ws-qs"><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><span>What happens to a queued registration if the clinic registers the same child before the phone syncs?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J3b/">J3b</a><span>How does the plan definition decide a dose is overdue, and what sets the date of the next one?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0b/">J4.0b</a><span>Where does the gateway read the consent from, and what does it do when the link has expired?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.1/">J4.1</a><span>Which AuditEvent fields let Onesa tell the family who looked at the record, and when?</span></li></ul>
<h3>Terms at those steps</h3><div class="ws-terms"><a href="glossary.html#term-client-registry" title="The Client Registry is the national authoritative source of health-specific person identity. Rules for minors and dependants differ by country.">Consent</a><a href="glossary.html#term-interoperability" title="Interoperability is the standards-based capability of heterogeneous information systems to communicate, exchange data, and use the exchanged information to execute functions effectively.">Interoperability</a><a href="glossary.html#term-terminology-service" title="The Terminology Service is a governed, publicly accessible service that manages, publishes, and provides access to the standardised terminologies, code systems, value sets, and concept maps used across the digital health ecosystem.">Terminology Service</a><a href="glossary.html#term-core-data-set" title="The elements a country agrees to record for a use case, each mapped to standard codes. Also called a minimum data set.">Core data set</a><a href="glossary.html#term-logical-information-model" title="The agreed structure of the data: elements, types and rules, independent of any software.">Logical information model</a><a href="glossary.html#term-snomed-ct" title="Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms is a structured clinical terminology standard for use in electronic health records.">SNOMED CT</a><a href="glossary.html#term-decision-support-engine" title="The Computable Decision Support Engine is a governed, shared application component that delivers context-appropriate, evidence-based guidance at the point of clinical decision-making by applying computable clinical rules and knowledge artefacts to person-specific health data.">Computable Decision Support Engine</a><a href="glossary.html#term-smart-guidelines" title="Standards-based, Machine-readable, Adaptive, Requirements-based, Testable Guidelines are a comprehensive set of reusable digital health components (e.g., interoperability standards, code libraries, algorithms, technical and operational specifications) that transform the guideline adaptation and implementation process to preserve fidelity and accelerate uptake. SMART Guidelines provide a five-step pathway to advance the adoption of best clinical and data practices, even if a country is not yet fully digital.">SMART Guidelines</a><a href="glossary.html#term-digital-adaptation-kit" title="Software-neutral L2 content: personas, workflows, core data dictionary, decision logic, indicators and requirements.">Digital adaptation kit</a><a href="glossary.html#term-dose-number-and-series" title="Which dose this is, out of how many in the schedule. Needed to work out what is due next.">Dose number and series</a><a href="glossary.html#term-expanded-programme-on-immunization" title="The national immunization programme.">Expanded Programme on Immunization</a><a href="glossary.html#term-international-patient-summary" title="A standard minimal health summary, including immunizations, readable across borders.">International Patient Summary</a><a href="glossary.html#term-hl7-fhir" title="FHIR is a standard for healthcare data exchange, published by HL7®">Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources</a><a href="glossary.html#term-implementation-guide" title="A FHIR specification for one use case: profiles, codes and tests. It can be adopted rather than authored.">Implementation guide</a><a href="glossary.html#term-profile" title="A FHIR resource tailored to a use case, for example by making some fields required.">Profile</a><a href="glossary.html#term-procurement-conditions" title="Requirements written into tenders, such as conformance to the national IG, that steer what suppliers build.">Procurement conditions</a><a href="glossary.html#term-application-programming-interface" title="A defined, documented way for one system to ask another for data.">Application programming interface</a><a href="glossary.html#term-global-digital-health-certification-network" title="WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network. A trust network so countries can verify each other's health documents. Countries onboard per use case.">Global Digital Health Certification Network</a><a href="glossary.html#term-trust-list" title="A published list of keys accepted as valid issuers. The GDHCN shares these between countries.">Trust list</a><a href="glossary.html#term-health-information-exchange" title="The layer that routes data securely between systems.">Health information exchange</a><a href="glossary.html#term-lifelong-health-record" title="The Lifelong Health Record (LHR) is one or more governed data repositories, whether physically consolidated or virtually federated, that collectively maintain a longitudinal, person-centred record of an individual's key health information across care settings and over their lifetime.">Lifelong Health Record</a></div>
